olivia_customer: Hey team — our per-model throughput lines in the Console collapsed to a single aggregated line around 2026-03-14T09:02Z after a deploy. API calls are still succeeding but customers report strange billing + latency spikes. Any ideas?

maya_support: hi @olivia_customer — sorry about that. Can you paste org id and a screenshot? Also did you change any tags/routing on your side? :eyes:

olivia_customer: Org 7832. Screenshot: https://secure-screenshots.example/7832/2026-03-14.png. We didn't touch routing. We did push a Grafana template change earlier in our infra but that should be independent of Redwood Console.

maya_support: copying @jamal_eng and @li_prod. Jamal, can you check the metric exporters / relabeler rollout for this org around that time? I'll start a billing check.

jamal_eng: looking at rollout logs now. There was a rollout of "metric-label-mapper" at 2026-03-14T08:55Z that applied a relabel rule: it renamed label `model` -> `model_id` and lowercased values. Quick grep from the exporter: 
```
2026-03-14T08:55:12Z INFO label-mapper: rule applied: {source: "model", target: "model_id", transform: "tolower"}
```
Initial hypothesis: dashboards still query by `model` so the per-model series appear empty.

li_prod: we deployed that mapper deliberately to normalize external ids. We assumed all Console queries had been migrated to `model_id`. Looks like two Console panels (per-model throughput + latency sparkline) still filter on `model`. Deployment notes missed the Console query update.

maya_support: can you confirm with PromQL? try: `sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[1m])) by (model)` and by `model_id`.

jamal_eng: ran both. `by(model)` returns zero series. `by(model_id)` returns normal time series for each model_id. So metric data is present, just relabeled. Example outputs: 
```
# by(model) -> empty
# by(model_id) -> model_id="gptx-120", value=42rps; model_id="gptx-60", value=12rps
```
So Console panels that rely on `model` end up showing no lines.

olivia_customer: Understood. But why did we see billing spikes? Billing should be per-org or per-route, not per-dashboard label. Customers got charged ~30% more yesterday.

jamal_eng: tracing/billing check: the itemized billing job aggregates token counts by label `model` for per-model breakdowns. When `model` was missing, aggregation fell back to `unknown_model` bucket. Some UI caches then double-counted `unknown_model` when merging cached snapshots with recent batch - this is a bug in the billing UI merge code. The raw usage DB is correct; the UI mis-aggregation produced the spike. We are opening a finance reconciliation ticket.

li_prod: rollback of the label-mapper was executed at 2026-03-14T09:03Z (rollback id: lbm-20260314-02). However dashboards remained stale because Grafana panels cache and predefined queries still referenced `model`. I pushed an emergency dashboard patch that supports both labels using label_replace: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[1m])) by (model) + sum(label_replace(sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[1m])) by (model_id), "model", "$1", "model_id", "(.*)" ) )
```
Patch PR: https://git.redwood/infr/PR-4123

maya_support: olivia — can you refresh the Console and confirm per-model lines return? Also we've opened SUP-3321 to reconcile any billing UI spikes with Finance.

olivia_customer: refreshed the dashboard — per-model lines are back and match expected traffic now. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

jamal_eng: follow-ups: (1) add a deploy checklist item for label renames that includes Console query audit, (2) make Console queries resilient to label aliases (use label_replace fallback), (3) postmortem + customer note. I'll create the runbook and assign owners.

maya_support: created SUP-3321; tagging finance and comms for reconciliation and customer email.

sre_bot: Deploy rollback complete: metric-label-mapper @ 1768abcd (status: success)

li_prod: really sorry for the disruption. We'll coordinate label migrations with product and eng to avoid silent console regressions. Closing after postmortem + reconciliation.
